b18: Akar masalah: satu `max-age=86400` dipakai untuk browser dan CDN sekaligus, tanpa mekanisme purge. Perbaikan: (1) Pisahkan TTL. Untuk rute katalog publik pakai `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, s-maxage=86400, stale-while-revalidate=60, stale-if-error=3600`. (2) Tag respons: `Surrogate-Key: product:sku-42 catalog` (Cloudflare `Cache-Tag`). (3) Saat admin menyimpan, commit DB dulu, lalu hapus key Redis terkait, lalu tulis event outbox yang memanggil purge-by-tag di CDN. Purge dijalankan setelah commit, dengan retry, supaya tidak terjadi race yang mengisi ulang cache dengan data lama. (4) Tambahkan `ETag` untuk revalidasi 304. Untuk insiden sekarang, lakukan purge manual URL/tag produk itu; karena mengubah CDN produksi, ini butuh persetujuan. Browser yang sudah menyimpan versi 24 jam tetap tidak bisa dipurge, jadi informasikan ke tim. Pastikan rute checkout/cart/akun tetap `private, no-store`, dan hindari `Vary: Cookie`. Verifikasi: `curl -sI https://<host>/produk/sku-42`, cek header dan `Age`/`cf-cache-status`, lalu ubah harga di staging dan pastikan perubahan tampil dalam ≤60 detik.
b22: Root cause: a plain `ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY` takes a SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE lock on `orders` (and on the referenced table) and scans all 30M rows to validate. Checkout INSERTs and UPDATEs queued behind it. If the ALTER first waited on a long transaction, every new query also queued behind the waiting lock. Fix (each production DDL step needs L4 approval): (1) `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_orders_customer_id ON orders(customer_id);` on the referencing column, outside a transaction. (2) `SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT fk_orders_customer FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers(id) NOT VALID;` This is a brief lock and checks only new rows. (3) Find orphans first with `SELECT count(*) FROM orders o LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.id=o.customer_id WHERE o.customer_id IS NOT NULL AND c.id IS NULL;` and clean them up. (4) `ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT fk_orders_customer;` takes SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, so writes continue. Retry if lock_timeout trips. Watch blockers via `pg_locks`/`pg_stat_activity` and lint the migration with the DDL safety checker.
b26: I won't edit `SRS_Final.docx` directly. It's a generated output, and the next regeneration would silently overwrite a hand edit with 99.5% again. (5) Run `validate --strict`, then regenerate through the same generator into `docs/output`. (6) Re-approve with an approver other than the owner. b30: Not ready. 100% on a set you tuned 15 times measures overfitting, not quality: the set became the training data. With 40 items the confidence interval is about ±15%. Before shipping: (1) Freeze a blind holdout the team has never seen, at least 100-300 stratified items, version it with dataset_vX.Y and a SHA-256 hash, and check that no IDs or few-shot examples leak from the dev set. (2) Cover all 6 archetypes: normal, ambiguous, abstention (must refuse), negative/contrast probes, adversarial (prompt injection, cross-tenant), and regressions. Report each category separately so a high overall score can't hide a 0% on tenant isolation. (3) Use deterministic graders first; calibrate any LLM judge at temp=0 and check its agreement with human labels (Cohen's kappa). (4) Compare baseline vs candidate on the same holdout, pairing samples (McNemar test), with a 95% Wilson interval. Any safety regression blocks the release. Run `ai_eval_gate.py --score-rag` and `--compare-rag` offline. Live paid sweeps need approval and a budget cap. The report lists what was measured and what is NOT_RUN.

b38: Three blockers. (1) The refresh token in AsyncStorage is plaintext and readable on rooted or backed-up devices. Store it in Keychain/Keystore (e.g. `react-native-keychain` with `ACCESSIBLE.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY`, or `expo-secure-store`), pin the version after `npm view`, set `allowBackup="false"`/`dataExtractionRules`, use rotating server-side refresh tokens, and migrate and delete the old AsyncStorage key on upgrade. (2) `if (await LocalAuth.authenticate()) setUnlocked(true)` is a client-side boolean that Frida or a patched JS bundle can bypass. Bind biometrics to a key: store the token under biometric access control (`accessControl: BIOMETRY_CURRENT_SET`, or BiometricPrompt with a Keystore `CryptoObject`), so a successful prompt is what releases the secret, and invalidate it when biometric enrollment changes. (3) `usesCleartextTraffic="true"` in the main manifest also ships in release. Set it to `false` in `src/main` and allow HTTP for localhost/10.0.2.2 only through `src/debug/res/xml/network_security_config.xml`. Verify: run `mobile_release_gate.py --scan .`, inspect the merged manifest of the release build, and test on a real device: upgrade migration, keychain, biometric re-enrollment.
b42: Alasan itu keliru. Docker menulis rule iptables sendiri (chain DOCKER) yang dievaluasi sebelum ufw, sehingga `5432:5432` dan `6379:6379` terbuka ke `0.0.0.0` dan bisa diakses dari internet walaupun `ufw deny`. Redis tanpa auth bisa langsung jadi RCE. Perbaikan di compose: hapus `ports` untuk db dan redis, lalu letakkan keduanya di network `internal: true` yang hanya dijangkau app. Kalau butuh akses admin, pakai `"127.0.0.1:5432:5432"` lewat SSH tunnel. Lengkapi dengan Redis `requirepass`/ACL, password DB dari secret, user non-root, `mem_limit`, healthcheck, dan log rotation. Verifikasi read-only: `docker ps --format '{{.Ports}}'`, `ss -tlnp | grep -E '5432|6379'`, lalu `nc -zv <ip-publik> 5432` dari host luar (harus gagal), dan `ops_hardening_verifier.py --check-compose docker-compose.prod.yml`. Penerapan ke produksi (`docker compose up -d`) butuh persetujuan L4 dan jendela waktu, karena koneksi ulang app perlu dicek. Port sempat terbuka, jadi periksa log autentikasi dan rotasi kredensial DB/Redis.

b54: Treat this as an active incident: the URL is public, so hiding it in the bundle is no control. (1) Scope it, read-only: confirm the route and handler (`file:line`), what data it exports (PII? all tenants?), and search access logs for `/internal/export-all` with status 200, unusual IPs and response sizes. (2) Contain, with L4 approval: block it at the edge right away (`location ^~ /internal/ { deny all; }`, WAF rule or kill switch). (3) If logs show exports, or you can't rule them out, start breach triage with Legal/DPO under the UU PDP 3×24h clock. Rotate any tokens or keys the endpoint exposed. (4) Fix the root cause on the server: authenticate, authorize admin with a server-side role check, scope by tenant, rate-limit and audit-log the export. Removing it from the bundle is hygiene, not the fix. (5) Lock in a regression test showing 401/403 for anonymous and non-admin users. (6) Add a CI route-policy check so new routes deny by default and a blameless postmortem.
